G. Fox), with no per-language phonology statement and no stress marking; §3.1.2 p.74 says transcription is 'a broad phonetic transcription. No attempt at phonemic analysis has been made'. The only 'stressed/unstressed syllables' mentions are footnotes to reflex tables (e.g. p.39 fn 3 'In unstressed syllables') attached to Orap, Petarmur, Larevat and other rows, never to the Mpotovoro row (its footnotes are 4 'R…
Nothing; sound inventory and wordlist only, and the doculect is filed under Vovo, not Mpotovoro.

sources.note: Abstract only (Crossref record): no tone content. The abstract names 'a group of four languages spoken along the north coast—Nese, Vovo, Botovro, and Vao—in which final vowels are retained if the vowel in the preceding syllable was high' and proposes 'that paragogic vowels were added after all retained final consonants, that a sonority-driven stress shift moved stress from a high penult to a more sonorous nonhigh final vowel, and that only then were final unstressed vowels deleted' — i.e. a reconstructed (diachronic) penultimate stress with sonority-driven shift for the Nese-Vovo-Botovro-Vao…
